title: SEC0: pipelining check only inspects BufReader buffer, not kernel socket buffer
description:
File: crates/reader/src/session/lifecycle.rs:423
Issue: The pipelining guard uses reader.buffer().is_empty() which only inspects data already pulled into the BufReader's in-process buffer. If the client sends STARTTLS followed immediately by post-STARTTLS commands, and the pipelined bytes arrive at the kernel socket buffer after read_line() has consumed the STARTTLS line but before buffer() is called, they will not be in the BufReader buffer at check time. The guard will pass, the server sends 382, and the plaintext pipelined bytes are then handed to the TLS handshake layer, corrupting the handshake. RFC 4642 §2.2 requires that pipelined commands after STARTTLS result in connection closure; this implementation cannot reliably enforce that.
Impact: Under a race window, a client can pipeline commands after STARTTLS without triggering the guard. The pipelined plaintext bytes reach the TLS acceptor, which interprets them as TLS ClientHello data, causing a failed or incorrect handshake. A malicious client could also use this to corrupt session state after upgrade.
